## Complete ordered inventory

### 1. Unused optional-metric verifier support

- Changed code: `instrumentation/jmx-metrics/library/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/jmx/rules/MetricsVerifier.java:25-97,134` adds `requiredMetrics`, `addOptional`, and forwarding logic, although the PR has no `addOptional` caller.
- Closest compliant example: the base implementation of the same file at `MetricsVerifier.java:24-76,109` stores assertions in one map and derives required names from its keys.
- Frequency: unique
- Disposition: avoidable
- Applicable rules and precedence: Java test guidance and Java style guidance are path-specific; the repository's focused-change and maintainability guidance is generic. No path-specific rule requires optional assertion support.
- Why the example complies: it keeps the existing fluent verifier behavior, uses the established data structure, and contains only behavior exercised by callers.
- Why avoidable: every new Trino assertion uses `add()`, so the added API, set, branch, and forwarding method do no job in this PR.
- Rule-conflict gate: repository, Java-style, Java-test, and generic minimal-change rules were checked. No rule requires the unused API or state. Restoring the base implementation complies with every applicable rule.
- Fix commit: `5d76e9857cfa847a7149e3fcac753b1831d3a6b3`
- Validation: `./gradlew :instrumentation:jmx-metrics:library:compileTestJava` passed.

### 2. Experimental prefix on the registry model filename

- Changed code: `instrumentation/jmx-metrics/model/experimental-trino.yaml:1-147` and `instrumentation/jmx-metrics/library/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/jmx/rules/TrinoTest.java:66` use the runtime target prefix for the Weaver registry filename.
- Closest compliant example: `instrumentation/jmx-metrics/library/src/main/resources/jmx/rules/experimental-cassandra.yaml:1` remains experimental at runtime, while `instrumentation/jmx-metrics/model/cassandra.yaml:1` and `CassandraTest.java:42,65` use the concise registry filename. Kafka Connect follows the same split at `experimental-kafka-connect.yaml:1`, `model/kafka-connect.yaml:1`, and `KafkaConnectTest.java:125,145`.
- Frequency: unique
- Disposition: avoidable
- Applicable rules and precedence: the same-component JMX model layout is the most specific naming convention; Java test guidance governs the test reference; generic repository consistency applies last.
- Why the example complies: both established experimental targets preserve `experimental-` for the runtime rule while naming the registry model after the target itself.
- Why avoidable: Trino can follow the same split without changing its runtime target name or behavior.
- Rule-conflict gate: repository, Java-test, JMX model-layout, and generic rules were checked. The Cassandra and Kafka Connect exemplars agree, no more-specific rule requires the registry prefix, and the renamed model plus matching test reference complies with every applicable rule.
- Fix commit: `50a0105081c7cae9a780a4be70238dc4c767073a`
- Validation: `./gradlew :instrumentation:jmx-metrics:library:test --tests io.opentelemetry.instrumentation.jmx.rules.TrinoTest` passed.

### 3. Version-pinned YAML editor directive

- Changed code: source `instrumentation/jmx-metrics/model/experimental-trino.yaml:1` adds `# yaml-language-server: $schema=...weaver/v0.24.2/...`; after finding 2's rename, the line was at `instrumentation/jmx-metrics/model/trino.yaml:1`.
- Closest compliant example: `instrumentation/jmx-metrics/model/cassandra.yaml:1` and `instrumentation/jmx-metrics/model/wildfly.yaml:1` begin directly with registry content and rely on the component manifest and Weaver test integration.
- Frequency: unique
- Disposition: avoidable
- Applicable rules and precedence: JMX model and metadata-YAML form is topic-specific; generic consistency and minimal-change guidance applies afterward; Java rules do not apply.
- Why the example complies: the established models are consumed through `model/manifest.yaml` and validated through the same Weaver integration without a file-local editor directive.
- Why avoidable: the comment does not participate in registry processing and introduces a separate, stale Weaver version pin.
- Rule-conflict gate: repository, JMX model-format, metadata-YAML, and generic rules were checked. No more-specific rule requires the editor comment, the exemplars comply with the registry form, and removing it complies with every applicable rule.
- Fix commit: `2d05af05eba69b6030d7912aef5b7b6514ad02c0`
- Validation: `./gradlew :instrumentation:jmx-metrics:library:test --tests io.opentelemetry.instrumentation.jmx.rules.TrinoTest` passed.
